proposals.name: Causal-mechanism explanation
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 how explicitly the comment lays out a specific causal chain ('because X, then Y, therefore Z') connecting the proposed action to the outcome it warns about or advocates for. A 10 gives a concrete, falsifiable, multi-step mechanism (e.g., a specific biological, procedural, or administrative pathway) rather than a conclusion alone. A 0 states a position or conclusion (support/oppose/agree) with no chain of reasoning connecting the rule to the claimed effect at all -- pure assertion or bare agreement.
proposals.rationale: R29 (Kirtland's Warbler) spells out the exact mechanism -- losing funding removes cowbird-parasitism control, which caused near-extinction before and would again -- while R48 (mine training) explains how removing District Manager authority breaks the accident-data-driven feedback loop that lets training keep pace with hazards; both are dense_high_card_low. By contrast R11 (MFA tax letter) and R28 (AASHTO extension request), both dense_low_card_high, state a position/request with no causal chain at all -- exactly the kind of unexplained assertion a scorecard bank built on presence-of-position might over-credit.

proposals.name: Independent/original evidentiary support
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment supplies verifiable data, measurements, test results, or independently gathered facts, as opposed to merely restating the notice or citing existing law/regulation text. A 10 presents original quantitative or empirical evidence gathered specifically to support the claim. A 0 offers no independent evidence at all -- only assertions, restated law, or unquantified characterizations.
proposals.rationale: R32 (Toyota) supplies original pull-force test measurements (26.9N, 114.4N, 306.8N) directly answering the agency's technical question, and R59 (tart citrus assessment) walks through an explicit expenditure calculation -- both dense_high_card_low. By contrast R43 (Iowa DOJ) proposes a specific $500,000 threshold with no supporting data on report volumes at that level, and R05 (NASACT) lists administrative burdens without quantifying any of them -- both dense_low_card_high, suggesting the scorecard rewards the topic of 'burden/threshold' without requiring it be evidenced.

proposals.name: Identifies a specific factual/technical inconsistency in the proposal
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment names and explains a concrete inconsistency, error, or gap between the proposed rule/notice and outside facts, cited service documents, or the agency's own stated rationale. A 10 identifies the exact inconsistency and its practical consequence for the rule. A 0 identifies no inconsistency and simply accepts or restates the notice's framing.
proposals.rationale: R40 (Orbital ATK) shows the NPRM misattributes root cause -- its own root-cause analysis found the LPT blade failure, not the bearing failure, was primary, which changes the appropriate compliance basis -- and R55 (Meggitt buckle SB) shows the proposed AD treats exactly 0.125 inch as unacceptable while the cited Service Bulletin lists it as acceptable. Both are concrete, checkable inconsistencies that a careful analyst would flag as substantive engagement with the rule's actual text.

proposals.name: Engages and rebuts the strongest counterargument
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment explicitly names the strongest argument or justification for the opposite position and directly rebuts it point by point. A 10 identifies the specific counter-rationale (legal, technical, or policy) and dismantles it with reasoning. A 0 states a position with no acknowledgment that any opposing view or justification exists.
proposals.rationale: R48 (mine training) explicitly names and rebuts the Appointments Clause/APA argument for stripping District Manager authority, explaining why the authority is administrative rather than 'significant regulatory power.' By contrast, purely supportive comments like R21 (coral habitat) and R51 (shrimp moratorium) -- both dense_high_card_low or dense_low_card_high respectively -- state a position with zero engagement with any counterview, showing this dimension is independent of which model favors the comment and worth scoring on its own.

proposals.name: Quantified, decision-relevant impact analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment translates its concern or support into concrete, checkable numbers (dollars, rates, timeframes, population counts) tied to the specific decision at hand. A 10 gives an itemized, traceable numeric analysis relevant to the exact provision at issue. A 0 characterizes impact only in general, unquantified terms.
proposals.rationale: R59 (tart citrus) walks through last year's expenditures minus the removed fruit-fly-program cost to justify a specific new rate, and R33 (Medicare Part B teachers) grounds its request in concrete figures -- 35,000 retirees, a plan running since 2007, a 17-year cost-containment role. Both dense_high_card_low. By contrast R04 ('not enough effort') and R45 ('must be protected... for the greater good') give no figures tied to the actual decision at all.

proposals.name: First-hand expertise applied to the rule's specific mechanics
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the commenter's demonstrated personal/professional experience is used to make a concrete, technically specific judgment about how the rule actually works, rather than merely being asserted as a credential. A 10 shows expertise driving a specific operational judgment call (e.g., a precise recommendation grounded in lived technical detail). A 0 states credentials or affiliation but never connects them to any specific judgment about the rule's mechanics.
proposals.rationale: R19 (Black Sea Bass) uses 30 years of charter fishing plus a marine biology degree to argue specifically for bag limits over minimum size limits, explaining hooking and swim-bladder mortality in released fish; R39 (flight training) directly compares Part 141 vs. 142 performance standards from the commenter's own training and instruction experience. Both dense_high_card_low, showing dense may track expertise-in-use rather than expertise-as-signature.

proposals.name: Traces downstream/second-order consequences
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment reasons at least one causal step beyond the rule's immediate, stated effect -- e.g., how an initial effect cascades onto third parties, markets, or future behavior. A 10 traces a multi-step cascade explicitly. A 0 addresses only the rule's most immediate, obvious effect with no further-order reasoning.
proposals.rationale: R20 (hot air balloon medical certification) traces a cascade from mandatory 2nd-class medicals to a shortage of certifying doctors to a training bottleneck to industry contraction, proposing a phased alternative; R48 (mine training) traces removed local authority to rigid uniform training to lagging behind hazards to elevated injury/fatality risk. By contrast R38 (VMS monitoring) raises pointed objections without tracing any further consequence.

proposals.name: Independent analysis beyond restating the notice or statute
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on how much the comment adds independent synthesis, critique, or judgment beyond paraphrasing the NPRM's own language or quoting the statute back at the agency. A 10 shows substantial independent cross-examination of the proposal's premises. A 0 is primarily a restatement of the rule's own summary or statutory language followed by a bare statement of agreement/disagreement.
proposals.rationale: R42 (NOSB organic standards) independently cross-examines the celery-powder nitrate loophole against OFPA's own prohibition and contrasts US methionine policy with the EU's welfare-linked alternative -- clear independent synthesis (dense_high_card_low). By contrast R11 (MFA) largely restates the proposed regulation's stated intent in near-identical language before declaring agreement (dense_low_card_high).

proposals.name: Concrete, checkable stakes vs. generic sentiment
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment describes who is actually affected and how, in specific, checkable terms (a named program, population count, operational detail), rather than invoking a general value ('protect the environment,' 'support small business') with no particulars. A 10 gives specific, verifiable stakes tied to the rule's actual mechanics. A 0 offers only generic value language with no particulars.
proposals.rationale: R46 (LA County DHS) cites 600,000 unique patients/year across four hospitals including two Level One trauma centers, tied to a specific payment-methodology provision; R33 cites 35,000 retired teachers on a named plan since 2007. Both dense_high_card_low. By contrast R45 ('must be protected... for the greater good... not just a few') states a value with no specifics of who, what, or how.

proposals.name: Load-bearing precise use of technical terminology
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment's technical/domain language is load-bearing for the argument -- i.e., removing the precise term or figure would remove the argument's force -- versus decorative technical-sounding language that doesn't actually change or support the specific claim. A 10 turns on an exact technical distinction that is the entire substance of the objection. A 0 uses jargon or technical references that could be deleted without weakening the argument.
proposals.rationale: R55 (Meggitt buckle) turns entirely on the boundary condition 'equal to 0.125 inch' vs. 'greater than 0.125 inch' -- the precise number is the whole objection; R47 (International Aero Engines) turns on precise engine-model nomenclature (which models had suspect bearings installed) to justify narrowing the applicability list. In both, the technical precision is not decorative -- it IS the argument.

proposals.name: Explicit evidence-to-requested-remedy linkage
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment draws an explicit, traceable line from the evidence or reasoning it presents to the exact provision, number, or action it asks the agency to change. A 10 shows the requested remedy derived transparently, step by step, from the stated evidence. A 0 presents evidence/complaint and a specific ask as disconnected pieces, with no traceable link between them.
proposals.rationale: R59 derives its requested $0.02 rate step by step from the stated expenditure figures -- a fully traceable link from evidence to ask (dense_high_card_low). By contrast R23 (FDA youth tobacco survey) raises scattered methodological/privacy objections but its ultimate demand ('just a waste of government funding' since 2009) is never connected point-by-point back to the specific data-collection provisions it complains about (dense_high_card_low as well, showing this dimension can explain within-bucket variance too).

proposals.name: Acknowledges limits of own evidence or expertise
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment explicitly flags uncertainty, gaps in its own knowledge, or the provisional nature of a claim, rather than presenting all assertions with uniform, unqualified confidence. A 10 gives specific, honest hedging tied to a real gap in the commenter's evidence. A 0 makes sweeping, unqualified claims with total confidence despite no stated basis for that certainty.
proposals.rationale: R09 (supersonic aircraft noise) explicitly hedges: 'I can't say for sure, because I have little data to work with,' while still making its case (dense_low_card_high, showing this quality can go unrewarded by the scorecard). By contrast R34 (Scarlet Macaw) flatly asserts the listing 'is not going to help the wild population' with no acknowledged uncertainty about the underlying conservation science (dense_high_card_low), showing this dimension cuts across both buckets rather than tracking either model directly.

proposals.name: Comparative/analogical grounding in a real precedent
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment supports its position by pointing to a specific, verifiable precedent, prior case, or parallel jurisdiction/standard -- not a vague appeal to 'other places do it differently.' A 10 names a specific, checkable comparator and explains the relevant difference it implies for this rule. A 0 offers no comparative grounding at all.
proposals.rationale: R42 (NOSB) names the EU's specific poultry-welfare standard (slower-growing breeds, more space per bird) as the real alternative to synthetic methionine, and R03 (Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon) cites Castillo v. City of Las Vegas, 195 P.3d 870, as precedent for compensating sentimental-value losses -- both concrete, checkable comparators that ground the requested change.

proposals.name: Internal consistency between premises and requested remedy
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment's concrete ask actually follows from, and does not exceed or contradict, its own stated premises and evidence. A 10 shows every argument building toward a single, matched conclusion with no scope drift. A 0 shows the final ask is broader than, unrelated to, or in tension with the specific reasoning that preceded it.
proposals.rationale: R48 (mine training) keeps its legal rebuttal, safety rationale, and specific proposal mutually reinforcing throughout -- premises and ask match exactly. By contrast R23 (FDA youth tobacco survey) argues specific methodological/consent objections but concludes with a much broader claim ('just a waste of government funding' since 2009) that exceeds what the preceding argument actually established -- a scope mismatch between evidence and remedy.

proposals.name: Substantive novelty beyond the proposal's own preamble
proposals.instruction: Score 0-10 on whether the comment supplies information, an argument, or a consideration that is not already contained in or obvious from the proposed rule's own preamble/summary -- i.e., whether it tells the agency something it did not already say. A 10 introduces genuinely new information or a new line of analysis. A 0 substantially restates the notice's own description of the proposal and states a position with nothing added.
proposals.rationale: R32 (Toyota) supplies original pull-force test data that resolves a technical question the notice itself left open, and R26 (Black-capped Petrel Working Group) brings field-level population, genetic, and habitat information from working scientists that goes beyond the agency's own Species Status Assessment framing. Both dense_high_card_low. By contrast R11 (MFA) restates the section's own stated intent in near-identical language before agreeing -- adding nothing the agency did not already know.

proposals.name: First-hand practitioner evidence from inside the regulated activity
proposals.instruction: Score how much of the comment's substance rests on knowledge the commenter could only have obtained by personally performing, operating, or living under the regulated activity. 10 = the comment reports specific things the commenter did, tested, measured, or repeatedly observed in that activity (a procedure run, a force measured, a condition encountered, how a practice actually plays out at the site), stated concretely enough that another practitioner could recognize or dispute them, and the recommendation turns on that experience. 5 = experience is claimed and lightly illustrated, but every substantive point could have been written without it. 0 = no experiential basis at all; the comment argues only from general knowledge, from the notice itself, or from an institutional position. Do not credit mere assertions of years of service or credentials; credit only transmitted observations.
proposals.rationale: R07 does not argue about the label at all -- it runs twist-and-pull, straight-pull, and single-stitch-pull tests, reports peak forces (26.9N, 114.4N, 306.8N), and compares the torn samples to labels recovered from the plant; that is evidence generated by the party in the best position to generate it. R14 is worth reading precisely because the writer trained under Part 142 and now instructs under Part 141, so the equivalence claim is a direct comparison rather than an inference. R56 supplies release-mortality experience from 30 years of fishing the actual stock at the actual depths. Against these, R38 and R40 take positions with no experiential basis whatsoever. A scorecard keyed to how a comment presents itself will over-read R38's polish and under-read R07 and R56.

proposals.name: Audits the agency's own figures, record, or arithmetic
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment tests the agency's stated justification against numbers or statements the agency itself placed in the record. 10 = the comment reworks the agency's arithmetic, or juxtaposes the proposal with the agency's own admission or its own prior rule, and shows the figures so the check is reproducible. 5 = the comment disputes a number but supplies no computation or source. 0 = the agency's figures are accepted or ignored entirely; the comment engages only at the level of preference.
proposals.rationale: R18 rebuilds the assessment-rate case line by line: the fruit-fly program is gone, so subtract $595,000 from last year's $751,148, compare against the $152,920 of proposed expenditures and the $282,572 reserve, and the reduced rate is shown to be affordable. R54 quotes EPA's own statement that it does not anticipate any HAP emission reductions from removing the exemption, then sets that against EPA's own multi-million-dollar cost estimate. R28 tests the order's two-year pool rule against reported inventory (92.9M lb in 1995 vs 108.2M lb today) and against import volumes. This is the cheapest possible check for an agency to act on and it is invisible to a criterion bank that asks whether a comment 'cites data' rather than whether it recomputes the agency's own.

proposals.name: Surfaces an affected class or case the proposal overlooked
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a specific category of person, entity, or operating situation that the proposal's text does not appear to contemplate, or contemplates wrongly, and shows the consequence of that gap. 10 = a concrete class or edge case is named, its exclusion or misclassification is tied to specific proposal language, and the resulting harm or absurdity is stated. 5 = a gap is gestured at but neither the class nor the consequence is made concrete. 0 = the comment discusses only the population the notice already addresses.
proposals.rationale: R45 makes one point and it is a real one: the listing would convert existing lawful owners of long-domesticated birds into violators overnight, a class the proposal appears to have reasoned past. R05, for all its heat, ends on a defect nobody else would report -- the intake form's self-identification list has no entry for the person the program exists to compensate. R10 finds two more: owners who did not reside at the property continuously, and extended family whose individual losses are not separately compensable. R57 supplies the mirror case on the industry side, an operator flying under 30 hours per year against a compliance clock derived from 200-300 hours per month. Coverage gaps are the highest-value thing a comment can find and nothing about their presentation makes them look impressive.

proposals.name: States the causal mechanism linking the rule to its effect
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment names the pathway by which the provision produces the outcome it predicts. 10 = the biological, economic, or procedural chain is spelled out step by step in enough detail that the agency could check or break it, and the requested change attacks a specific link in that chain. 5 = a mechanism is named but left as a phrase, with no steps. 0 = an outcome is asserted (it will help, it will destroy, it is essential) with no pathway at all.
proposals.rationale: R32 does not merely say the warbler needs money -- it explains that habitat provision alone is insufficient because brown-headed cowbirds, whose range expanded post-settlement, parasitize the nests, so withdrawing intervention funding produces nesting failure rather than slow decline. R30 identifies the exact loophole mechanism (celery grown under high nitrate fertilizer, concentrated into powder, admitted as a nonorganic agricultural ingredient since 2007) and separately explains synthetic methionine as the input that makes confinement production feasible. R56 gives the mortality pathway for released undersize fish: hooking damage, swim bladder damage at depth, predation. Compare R23 and R48, which assert stakes with no mechanism; a bank that scores 'is the comment substantive' cannot separate these.

proposals.name: Rebuts the agency's own stated rationale on its terms
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment locates the reason the agency gave for the proposal and argues directly against that reason. 10 = the agency's stated justification is identified accurately and met head-on with a counter-argument or counter-evidence addressed to it. 5 = the agency's rationale is acknowledged but the response changes the subject to the commenter's own concerns. 0 = the rationale is never engaged; the comment states a position as if the proposal had no reasoning behind it.
proposals.rationale: R51 does the hardest version of this: MSHA framed the revision as statutory alignment under the Appointments Clause and the APA, and USW answers that framing directly -- District Managers exercise a delegated administrative function, not significant regulatory power -- before returning to hazard evidence. R25 contests the Service's reading of its own Species Status Assessment and argues the data support endangered rather than threatened, i.e. it attacks the determination's basis, not just its conclusion. R17 explains why the agency's guidance-versus-rulemaking choice matters in a way the agency would not know: Kentucky law (KRS 13A.130) bars the Cabinet from regulating by guidance document, so uncodified guidance is inoperable for the implementing state. Answering the rationale is what makes a comment usable in the response-to-comments; restating a preference is not.

proposals.name: Applies a controlling standard to the facts rather than citing it
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment takes a governing legal, scientific, or professional standard and works the proposal's facts through it. 10 = the standard is named, its elements are identified, and the proposal's facts are matched against those elements to show fit or misfit, with the mismatch driving the recommendation. 5 = a standard is invoked and the conclusion asserted, with the application left implicit. 0 = authority or the notice is quoted or summarized at length in place of analysis, or no standard is engaged.
proposals.rationale: R43 is a clean instance: the writer states the IUCN Reintroduction Guidelines constraint (do not reintroduce until the original cause of extirpation is addressed), applies it to Guam's brown tree snakes, then applies the conservation-introduction provision to the Palmyra site assessment and to the release and post-release monitoring elements one by one. R25 does the same with the statutory threatened-versus-endangered line and the resiliency/redundancy/representation framework. The contrasting failure mode is visible in R12 and R26, which reproduce large stretches of the Federal Register narrative and the procedural history and then stop short of applying anything to them -- a shape that reads as rigorous and analyzes little.

proposals.name: Supplies a workable alternative, not just opposition or support
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment gives the agency something it could actually adopt instead of what it proposed. 10 = a specific alternative is laid out -- the instrument, threshold, sequence, or the documents and definitions to be amended are named -- and its feasibility is argued. 5 = a direction is suggested (be more flexible, do it differently) without specifying the alternative. 0 = support or opposition with no alternative offered.
proposals.rationale: R58 is the strongest: it proposes accrediting private certification bodies under ISO 17065, points to the National Organic Program's Accredited Certifying Agents under 7 CFR 205.501 as the existing precedent, and then names exactly which documents change (QAD 1000, 1001, 1012 and its checklist) and which Part 62 definitions need expanding. R56 proposes swapping the regulatory instrument entirely -- drop minimum size limits, hit the same biomass objective through bag limits -- and argues why that dominates on discard mortality. R33 supplies a phased alternative with a passenger-count threshold, an examiner-capacity fix, and a data-review point. R47 specifies both a penalty and an NMFS-attended audit for the first three years. An alternative is what lets an agency move; bare opposition is not.

proposals.name: Ask serves more than the commenter's own burden or exposure
proposals.instruction: Score the beneficiary of the requested change as the comment itself frames it. 10 = the change would improve the rule's functioning for third parties, the protected resource, or the public, including where it plainly costs the commenter something. 5 = mixed: the ask helps the commenter but the stated reasons are about workability for everyone. 0 = the entire ask is relief for the submitter -- delay, exemption, a higher threshold, more time -- with the public-interest framing supplying no independent content.
proposals.rationale: R25 asks the Service to list the species in a MORE restrictive category than proposed and to add incidental-take prohibitions, which is an ask against the grain of what a petitioner would want if it were optimizing for itself. R51 argues for retaining an authority exercised over its own members' employers. R56 asks for a change that would reduce, not increase, what he may keep. Against those: R34's entire content is a request for 15 additional days; R02 asks that the reporting requirement be repealed or deferred to 2023 because it is expensive for the commenter's members; R29 asks that the threshold be raised tenfold so its own office files fewer forms. All three are courteous, correctly addressed, provision-anchored, and ask the agency for nothing but their own relief -- exactly the profile a criterion bank rewards.

proposals.name: Requested change is material, not a single-filer scope cleanup
proposals.instruction: Score how much would change if the agency granted the request. 10 = adoption would alter who is covered, protected, or burdened, or by how much -- the substantive reach or stringency of the rule moves. 5 = adoption would change how the rule operates for a definable group without changing its reach. 0 = the request is an editorial, applicability, or cross-reference correction whose consequences run essentially to the filer alone, however precisely stated.
proposals.rationale: R35 is precise, correct-looking, and cites exact model numbers -- and asks only that three engine designations be struck from an applicability list. R39 asks whether exactly 0.125 inch is acceptable, reconciling AD text against a service bulletin. Both are the kind of narrowly scoped, perfectly formatted request that scores well on any 'specific and actionable' criterion while barely moving the rule. Set against R30 (relisting of celery powder, excluded methods, synthetic methionine -- each of which changes what may be sold as organic), R27 (which forum prosecutes drug and DUI offenses on federal land, and whether enhancements and interlock survive), and R25 (which listing category applies). Materiality and actionability are different axes and a bank that scores only the second inverts them.

proposals.name: Original analysis dominates reproduction of material already in the record
proposals.instruction: Score the proportion of the comment's substance that is the commenter's own reasoning about the proposal, as against material the agency already possesses -- block quotation or paraphrase of the notice, recitation of procedural history, and description of the commenter's own organization. Judge analytic content, not layout or length. 10 = essentially all substance is the commenter's own analysis; recited material appears only where a specific passage is being attacked. 5 = roughly half is reproduced material that carries the reader to the analysis. 0 = the comment is largely a summary of what the agency proposed plus a description of who the commenter is, with a position stated at the end.
proposals.rationale: R12 reproduces a long passage of the Federal Register narrative and much of its own procedural framing before reaching its questions; R26 spends its length on stakeholder rosters, the geology background, and the history of its own prior comment letters. R16 and R50 both open with extended self-description (member counts, market share, program names) before the analysis begins. None of that is information the agency lacks. Compare R18 and R56, which start inside the problem and stay there, and R10, which is nothing but its own analysis, section by section. The reproduced material makes a comment look thorough while contributing nothing to the record.

proposals.name: Contributes site-, region-, or population-specific facts
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment supplies concrete facts tied to a named place, population, or operation, of a kind the agency is unlikely to already hold. 10 = specific local facts (named programs and their funding, counts and magnitudes for a defined population, named local ecological conditions, named local operating constraints) that materially bear on the proposal. 5 = a locality is named but the facts offered about it are generic. 0 = only national or generic claims. Score the facts, not the commenter's identity or standing.
proposals.rationale: R15 hands NHTSA the actual channel map for its own survey question: PSAs under station licensing, personal-injury advertising, FDOT's Ridesmart and CUTR grants, and the $2.50 motorcycle registration fee against 638,883 registered motorcycles with the FRTP dismantled and residual funds flowing to a general fund. That is information a national survey design cannot generate for itself. R11 gives CMS the operating scale behind its position -- 4,084 square miles, four acute hospitals including two Level One trauma centers, roughly 600,000 unique patients a year regardless of ability to pay. R31 supplies Big Island-only breeding, native-tree nest dependence, strawberry guava invasion, and ROD dieback. R28 supplies Michigan storage tonnage. Local facts are the scarce input in rulemaking and they arrive in unimpressive packaging.

proposals.name: Names a specific administrability defect from the complier's seat
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment identifies a concrete, mechanism-level reason the rule will fail or misfire in execution, tied to the provision that causes it. 10 = a specific execution defect is named -- a required field or category that does not exist, a licensing or supply constraint that makes compliance impossible on the stated timeline, a cost of participating that the rule declines to recognize -- and located in the text that creates it. 5 = a real implementation difficulty is described in general terms. 0 = burden is asserted without mechanism, or the comment never reaches implementation.
proposals.rationale: R46 identifies something only a vendor would know: the measures depend on standardized instruments, and copyright restrictions block vendors from supplying the content and managing its cost, so a measure can be adopted and still be unimplementable. R33 names the binding constraint on a 180-day compliance window -- the small pool of physicians certified to issue second-class medicals, plus DPE examiner capacity. R05, beneath the anger, reports that the claim intake path itself is the obstacle and that its self-identification list omits the claimant category. R10 notes that claim-preparation time and appraisal and expert costs are excluded from recoverable damages, which shapes who can actually use the program. Contrast R02, which asserts burden at length and then asks for repeal rather than naming a fixable defect.

proposals.name: Transmits aggregated practitioner knowledge, not membership claims
proposals.instruction: Score whether a collective is functioning as a source of evidence or as a claim to authority. 10 = the comment conveys what a body of practitioners collectively knows or actually does -- documented field practice, accumulated records, joint procedures already in operation -- so the collective's experience enters the record as testable content. 5 = a collective position is asserted with one or two concrete illustrations. 0 = the organization's size, market share, or membership is offered as the reason to credit the comment, with no collective knowledge transmitted. Score transmitted knowledge, not who the submitter is.
proposals.rationale: R25 puts 120 working-group members behind a specific evidentiary claim and points to the field reports and meeting notes that back it, including from the people who authored the original conservation plan -- the group is an evidence base. R27 does the same for practice rather than science: it describes the joint arrangements already running (a state law permitting deputization of USFS rangers, a national MOU template developed with western sheriffs, established case-routing to state prosecution) and reasons from how those actually work. R36 reports 17 years of administering coverage for 35,000 retirees and volunteers the plan as a demonstration site. Against these, R16 and R50 lead with 440 distributors, 85% of capacity, 93% of revenue, and world's largest trade association -- authority claims where knowledge should be.

proposals.name: Disagrees without imputing bad faith or conspiracy
proposals.instruction: Score whether disagreement is carried on the merits. 10 = the comment opposes strongly and never attributes corrupt, vindictive, or dishonest motive to the agency, its staff, or other parties; adverse characterizations, where made, are supported. 5 = one loaded rhetorical framing that does not carry the argument. 0 = the comment attributes bad motive as an argument (the rule exists to generate violations, the action is a vendetta by a cartel), attacks individuals, or leans on insinuation in place of evidence.
proposals.rationale: R21 is written by a genuinely qualified party -- A&P/IA, commercial and instrument rated, an aeronautical engineering and EE background, 6,000 hours -- and contains a real technical question about failure rates across TSO-C91 and C91a units, but it routes that through a claimed vendetta by the '406 ELT mafia' and an aside about firing a mechanic for incompetency, which converts checkable points into an accusation the agency cannot act on. R13 opens by asking whether the monitoring proposal exists to write more violations and closes on 'big brother', burying its one genuinely useful observation (charter vessels with substantial rockfish take are not required to carry VMS). R44 and R53 are grievance throughout. Formal cues -- credentials, structure, a clear ask -- survive intact in all four, so a bank keyed to those cues cannot discount them.

proposals.name: Marks the limits of its evidence and reasons from them
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment distinguishes what it knows from what it does not, and whether the recommendation follows from that distinction. 10 = the comment states where the evidence runs out, identifies the specific unknowns, and derives a recommendation that is responsive to the uncertainty (precaution, a specified disclosure, a question the agency must answer before proceeding). 5 = uncertainty is acknowledged in passing and does not affect the recommendation. 0 = uniform certainty regardless of basis, or hedging with no consequence attached.
proposals.rationale: R25 turns the gap into the argument: it flags assumptions the Service made despite missing information and reasons that a lack of information argues for the more conservative classification, so the uncertainty determines the ask rather than weakening it. R60 does the methodological version -- it does not assert the study is flawed, it names precisely what is undetermined (whether results will be published and in what form, whether IRB approval or exemption is sought, how sample representativeness will be ensured, whether stratification is planned) and ties each unknown to whether the instrument can support its conclusions, including the point that the preference questions cannot be evaluated without seeing the stimulus. Against these, R44 dismisses an entire data collection as not relevant and a waste, and R23 and R48 state certainty proportional to feeling rather than evidence.

proposals.name: Pinpointed rule-text correction
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies exact provisions, figures, definitions, or thresholds and proposes a precise textual correction; score 0 when it offers only a general opinion without locating the issue.
proposals.rationale: R17 identifies a threshold conflict between the proposed AD and service bulletin, while R59 proposes changes tied to numerous specific subsections.

proposals.name: Causal mechanism
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment clearly explains the chain linking a proposed requirement to a concrete safety, health, environmental, or economic consequence; score 0 when it asserts consequences without explaining how they arise.
proposals.rationale: R20 connects label removal, measured forces, stitching, and seatbelt strength; R42 explains how habitat loss plus cowbird parasitism produces nesting failure.

proposals.name: Quantified supporting evidence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment uses relevant numerical data, calculations, comparisons, or rates to support its position; score 0 when it provides no verifiable quantitative support.
proposals.rationale: R30 calculates expenditures, reserves, and the proposed assessment rate, while R11 compares inventories, imports, and historical storage levels.

proposals.name: Evidence applicability
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when cited studies, records, observations, or authorities are directly relevant to the affected population, technology, or regulatory question and their applicability is explained; score 0 when evidence is absent, irrelevant, or merely name-checked.
proposals.rationale: R18 relates reintroduction guidelines and conservation biology to the proposed release, while R32 draws on watershed-specific selenium monitoring and tissue data.

proposals.name: Implementation realism
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment maps the practical steps, resources, timing, personnel, or supply-chain conditions needed to implement the proposal; score 0 when it ignores implementation realities.
proposals.rationale: R26 identifies repair-station scarcity, utilization, logistics, and contractual effects; R49 details design, certification, testing, manufacturing, installation, training, and supply-chain steps.

proposals.name: Existing-rule interaction
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment accurately identifies overlap, conflict, redundancy, or complementarity with existing rules, standards, manuals, or programs and explains the consequence; score 0 when it treats the proposal in isolation.
proposals.rationale: R09 argues that the proposed inspection duplicates existing FAA inspection requirements, while R45 identifies duplication and sequencing problems across two proposed ADs.

proposals.name: Differentiated treatment
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment shows why impacts or appropriate requirements differ across relevant sizes, uses, locations, technologies, risk levels, or populations and proposes corresponding distinctions; score 0 when it assumes one uniform treatment fits all.
proposals.rationale: R22 distinguishes balloon operations by passenger capacity and use, while R26 distinguishes high-utilization engines from an exceptionally low-utilization aircraft.

proposals.name: Equivalent safeguard alternative
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment offers a concrete alternative that plausibly achieves the proposal’s protective objective and explains why it is equivalent or better; score 0 when it merely objects without an alternative.
proposals.rationale: R26 proposes inspections and life limits as an equivalent engine-safety approach, while R46 proposes bag limits instead of size limits and explains the mortality mechanism.

proposals.name: Monitoring and adaptation design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment specifies measurable monitoring, reporting, review triggers, corrective actions, or adaptive revisions that would reveal and address problems; score 0 when it offers no mechanism for learning or correction.
proposals.rationale: R12 proposes audit reporting, stricter consequences, and agency attendance during initial audits; R44 defends site-specific training changes based on inspections and accident data.

proposals.name: Explicit uncertainty treatment
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment distinguishes known facts from assumptions, identifies consequential data gaps, and explains how uncertainty should affect the rule or analysis; score 0 when it presents uncertain claims as settled.
proposals.rationale: R03 discusses uncertainty in population size, reproduction, and mortality estimates, while R40 challenges assumptions and interpretations made despite missing information.

proposals.name: Scope and applicability precision
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment carefully identifies which entities, models, activities, geographic areas, or conditions should be covered or excluded and supports those boundaries; score 0 when its requested scope is vague or overbroad.
proposals.rationale: R41 specifies the affected engine models and removes unsupported models, while R55 asks targeted questions about inspection lines, government inspectors, workloads, and sampling in Poland.

proposals.name: Tradeoff and side-effect analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment weighs the proposal’s benefits against costs, risks, displaced protections, or unintended effects and explains the relevant tradeoff; score 0 when it presents only one-sided approval or opposition.
proposals.rationale: R33 compares added compliance costs with claimed environmental benefit, while R22 addresses effects on pilots, doctors, training schools, insurers, and FAA administration.

proposals.name: Concrete administrative burden
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces burden to specific systems, forms, staffing, training, data, or recurring tasks and connects those burdens to a workable modification; score 0 when it uses only generic claims that compliance is burdensome.
proposals.rationale: R38 itemizes system development, data fields, testing, maintenance, and employee training, while R19 proposes specific alternatives for certification materials and timing.

proposals.name: Distributional consequence analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies which vulnerable, dependent, underserved, or differently situated groups bear distinct effects and explains the mechanism; score 0 when it invokes broad public interest without identifying affected groups.
proposals.rationale: R05 connects payment policy to safety-net hospitals and hundreds of thousands of patients, while R39 explains how formulary exclusions may affect patients who respond differently to medicines.

proposals.name: Proposal-specific engagement
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment addresses the actual proposal’s provisions, acknowledges relevant competing considerations, and makes prioritized actionable recommendations; score 0 when it is generic support, opposition, or emotional reaction untethered to the proposal.
proposals.rationale: R14 identifies a specific omission and proposes amendments across reporting, training, databases, and related policies, while R17 focuses on one concrete ambiguity instead of merely endorsing or opposing the AD.

proposals.name: Provision-level defect detection
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies an exact provision, figure, definition, or version conflict and proposes a precise correction; score 0 when it offers only a generic reaction with no identifiable textual defect.
proposals.rationale: R06, R28, and R41 show technically specific discrepancies that broad scorecards may miss.

proposals.name: Quantified reasoning tied to the rule
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when relevant numbers, calculations, comparisons, and assumptions directly support the requested change; score 0 when numbers are absent, unexplained, or merely rhetorical.
proposals.rationale: R18 and R56 connect numerical analysis or testing to concrete requests, while R31 illustrates quantitative risk reasoning.

proposals.name: Causal mechanism from provision to consequence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment traces a credible chain from the proposed provision through behavior or implementation to a safety, health, environmental, or administrative consequence; score 0 when it merely asserts that harm or benefit will occur.
proposals.rationale: R10, R48, and R52 explain mechanisms linking regulatory choices to mining safety, noise exposure, or species survival.

proposals.name: Implementation pathway and dependency analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment maps responsible actors, sequential steps, lead times, dependencies, and transition needs; score 0 when it gives no plausible account of how the proposal would operate.
proposals.rationale: R09, R29, and R37 identify repair capacity, medical-exam logistics, certification, testing, installation, and training dependencies.

proposals.name: Credible alternative meeting the regulatory objective
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment proposes a specific alternative, exception, phase-in, or substitute and explains why it can achieve the same objective with relevant tradeoffs; score 0 when it only supports or opposes the proposal.
proposals.rationale: R09 proposes inspections and life limits, R46 proposes bag limits, and R57 argues for an alternative training-equivalence period.

proposals.name: Risk-based scope tailoring
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies materially different affected subgroups or conditions and calibrates requirements, exemptions, or thresholds accordingly; score 0 when it applies one undifferentiated solution without explaining relevant differences.
proposals.rationale: R29 distinguishes balloon operations by passenger capacity, R28 distinguishes engine models, and R40 addresses nonstandard employment arrangements.

proposals.name: Cross-rule and system interaction
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies overlap, contradiction, gap, or sequencing with another rule, program, document, or process and specifies how to resolve it; score 0 when it analyzes the proposal in isolation.
proposals.rationale: R28 and R41 identify conflicts between related airworthiness directives, while R47 addresses interactions among certification procedures and permits.

proposals.name: Monitoring, learning, and trigger design
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment specifies what should be monitored, against which baseline, at what cadence, and what threshold or finding would trigger action; score 0 when it merely requests monitoring, review, or more data.
proposals.rationale: R20 describes post-release monitoring, R31 emphasizes trend and population-data review, and R58 proposes recurring audits with agency participation.

proposals.name: Evidence fit and source quality
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when empirical, scientific, or field evidence is relevant, identifiable, appropriately current, and directly applied to the claim; score 0 when the comment relies on generic citations, credentials, or unsupported anecdotes.
proposals.rationale: R23 connects watershed experience to selenium criteria, R44 uses species-specific conservation evidence, and R50 supplies relevant maintenance experience.

proposals.name: Uncertainty and limitation handling
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment separates established facts from assumptions, identifies alternative explanations or missing evidence, and calibrates its recommendation accordingly; score 0 when it is either categorically confident without support or vaguely claims uncertainty.
proposals.rationale: R31 discusses uncertainty in population and mortality estimates, R50 asks for missing failure-rate comparisons, and R48 explains measurement-data limitations.

proposals.name: Distributional impact and burden incidence
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies which groups bear risks or costs, which receive benefits, how impacts differ among them, and any mitigation; score 0 when it refers only abstractly to the public, fairness, or burden.
proposals.rationale: R40 examines precarious workers, R43 details burdens on state governments, and R60 discusses effects on retirees, plans, patients, and drug developers.

proposals.name: Operational burden grounded in workflow
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment describes concrete staffing, system, supply-chain, time, or cost burdens and their scale; score 0 when it merely labels a proposal costly, confusing, or burdensome.
proposals.rationale: R09 identifies the scarcity of qualified repair stations, R37 enumerates certification and installation work, and R43 describes reporting-system and training requirements.

proposals.name: Measurement validity and data integrity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment evaluates sampling, representativeness, incentives, privacy, bias, missingness, or instrument validity and links those issues to data usefulness; score 0 when it assumes that collected data will automatically be reliable.
proposals.rationale: R08 questions youth-survey honesty and consent, R36 addresses sample representativeness and survey design, and R23 discusses tissue-based versus water-column measures.

proposals.name: Legal authority and procedural safeguards
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies governing legal authority and applies it to specific proposed language, delegation, reporting, enforcement, or safeguards; score 0 when it invokes legality or rights only in general terms.
proposals.rationale: R07 examines equivalency and inspection authority, R21 identifies statutory reporting requirements, and R58 applies statutory data provisions to audit safeguards.

proposals.name: Balanced tradeoff analysis
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment acknowledges credible benefits and costs, explains the competing objectives, and gives a prioritized or conditional recommendation; score 0 when it is purely generic support or opposition.
proposals.rationale: R32 distinguishes legitimate trade from illegal imports, R48 weighs travel benefits against noise and carbon costs, and R55 balances access to medicines against formulary controls.

proposals.name: Attachment-forwarding cover-note boilerplate
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment begins with a short, stand-alone forwarding/transmittal line (e.g. 'See Attached', 'See attached file(s)', 'Please see attached comments of X') that is textually separate from, and precedes, the substantive letter that follows, rather than opening directly with substantive content. 10 = the comment opens with such a transmittal preamble before the real letter body begins. 0 = the comment has no transmittal preamble at all; substantive content starts in the first sentence.
proposals.rationale: The transmittal-preamble pattern is strongly associated with LOW dense scores despite high scorecard scores in this slice: ROW R18 (Louisiana Chemical Association, dense_pct=.274/card_pct=.782), ROW R50 (Food & Water Watch, dense_pct=.105/card_pct=.638), ROW R34 (Southern Shrimp Alliance, dense_pct=.166/card_pct=.618) and ROW R19 (Unlearn.AI, dense_pct=.122/card_pct=.563) all open with a 'See attached'-style line. This looks like a mechanical artifact of how a letter got filed, not a marker of the letter's substance.
proposals.upstream_parent: submission workflow: a staffer or paralegal at an organization pastes a finished PDF letter into a regulations.gov web form via a routine copy-paste habit, rather than composing text directly in the form

proposals.name: Formal itemized technical/regulatory rebuttal structure
proposals.instruction: Score the degree to which the comment is organized as a formal point-by-point regulatory rebuttal: addressed to a named official/office, broken into discrete numbered or lettered items, each citing a specific rule paragraph, CFR subsection, AD/docket number, or service-bulletin reference, with little connective persuasive narrative between points. 10 = the entire comment is such a structured technical-correction list (e.g. 'Comment No1... Page/Paragraph/Section... What is the FAA's proposed requirement...'). 0 = the comment is continuous persuasive prose with no addressee-directed itemized rule-section corrections.
proposals.rationale: Corporate airworthiness-directive-style itemized technical corrections score LOW dense in this slice: ROW R25 (International Aero Engines, dense_pct=.127), ROW R36 (Embraer, dense_pct=.336), ROW R40 (Meggitt vane-thickness comment, dense_pct=.293). Compliance staff are often the most technically expert commenters, so the format could co-occur with real expertise, yet dense appears to discount it regardless.
proposals.upstream_parent: the submitter is a regulated entity's engineering/compliance staff responding to a routine Airworthiness Directive or product-specific technical requirement as an established business process, not an independent stakeholder building a persuasive case

proposals.name: Single-ask brevity with minimal elaboration
proposals.instruction: Score how much of the comment consists of a short, single-purpose plea or statement of position (support/oppose) with little independent factual elaboration, data, or argumentative development beyond restating the ask and a one-line reason. 10 = the comment is essentially one short paragraph whose content is almost entirely 'I support/oppose this because [one general reason], please do X.' 0 = the comment develops multiple distinct facts, data points, or argumentative steps beyond the bare ask.
proposals.rationale: ROW R01 (sea-turtle moratorium plea, dense_pct=.429/card_pct=.976), ROW R11 (PA motorcycle-training complaint, dense_pct=.398/card_pct=.902) and ROW R17 (HHS abortion-coverage plea, dense_pct=.517/card_pct=.972) are all short, largely single-note pleas that score very high on the scorecard while dense scores them only mid-range, well below several longer or more elaborated comments in the slice.
proposals.upstream_parent: submitter engaged with the docket via a quick, low-effort action (e.g. a brief comment typed directly into a simple web form) reflecting low time investment rather than sustained analysis

proposals.name: Scanned/OCR text legibility (signal vs. noise)
proposals.instruction: Score the proportion of the comment's visible text that reads as coherent, grammatical, on-topic English prose, as opposed to garbled OCR fragments, single-word line breaks, stray characters, or illegible scanned-handwriting artifacts. 10 = the text is entirely clean, coherent prose throughout. 0 = the large majority of the visible text is unreadable noise or fragments with little or no recoverable meaning.
proposals.rationale: ROW R49 (handwritten scanned letter, almost entirely illegible OCR noise, dense_pct=.105, the lowest dense score in the whole slice) and ROW R50 (letter mangled into single-word-per-line fragments in its middle section, dense_pct=.105) sit at the very bottom of the dense distribution, while ROW R54 (a letter with visible OCR/margin-text noise bleeding into the paragraph flow but whose core argument remains fully legible) scores dense_pct=.880, near the top of the whole slice -- suggesting dense tracks legibility/extractability rather than a property of the argument itself.
proposals.upstream_parent: submission channel: physical, scanned, faxed, or handwritten mail versus born-digital electronic submission, and/or the docket back-end's PDF-to-text extraction quality

proposals.name: First-person credential or stake self-disclosure
proposals.instruction: Score how explicitly and prominently the comment establishes the writer's personal identity, credentials, professional role, or stake in the issue (e.g. 'I am a Professor...', 'I have X years of experience...', 'I represent...', naming a degree, certification, or affiliation) as a rhetorical move, independent of whether that identity is actually load-bearing for the argument's substance. 10 = the comment opens with or centers on an extended personal/professional credential or identity statement. 0 = the comment contains no self-identifying credential or stake language at all.
proposals.rationale: ROW R26 (a zoology professor's extensive credential paragraph, dense_pct=.901, near the very top of the slice) and ROW R33 (a Harbor School student/scuba-diver personal-identity narrative, dense_pct=.901) both pair heavy self-identification with very high dense scores; ROW R41 ('I have fished recreationally... and have a degree in Marine Biology', dense_pct=.662) shows the same pattern at a smaller scale.
proposals.upstream_parent: submitter's professional standing, expertise, or personal stake in the issue, and an instinct to lead with ethos-establishing credentials

proposals.name: Authority name-dropping / citation density
proposals.instruction: Score the density and prominence of named external authorities invoked in the comment -- cited reports, agencies, studies, statutes, or organizations named -- regardless of whether their substance is actually engaged, analyzed, or applied to a specific argument. 10 = the comment names or lists numerous external authorities/reports/institutions, even as a bare index or bibliography with no analysis attached. 0 = the comment makes no reference to any named external authority, study, or institution.
proposals.rationale: ROW R23 (a joint NHTSA CAFE comment that is literally an index of dozens of report titles -- CDC, EPA, National Academies, JD Power, National Geographic -- with almost no connecting analytical prose) still scores dense_pct=.626, well above its card_pct=.185; ROW R33 (which quotes the FAO and National Geographic by name) scores dense_pct=.901. Both show elevated dense tied to sheer citation volume rather than demonstrated synthesis.
proposals.upstream_parent: organizational resources: access to research staff, outside counsel, or a coalition's shared attachment library able to marshal many external citations regardless of whether they are substantively integrated into the argument

proposals.name: Meta-procedural commentary about the rulemaking process
proposals.instruction: Score how much of the comment is about the rulemaking PROCESS itself -- e.g. requesting an extension of the comment period, objecting to use of guidance documents instead of notice-and-comment rulemaking, or discussing procedural timing/authority -- rather than substantively engaging with the content of the proposed rule. 10 = the comment is primarily or entirely about process/procedure. 0 = the comment is entirely about the substance of the rule, with no procedural commentary.
proposals.rationale: ROW R51 (AASHTO's pure comment-period-extension request, with no engagement with the underlying NEPA rule's substance at all) scores dense_pct=.785, one of the higher dense scores in the slice despite card_pct=.334; ROW R48 (Kentucky Division for Air Quality, which argues at length that EPA should codify policy through notice-and-comment rulemaking rather than guidance memos) scores dense_pct=.539 while card_pct=.067 is the lowest card score in the entire slice.
proposals.upstream_parent: submitter is a repeat, institutionally sophisticated player (state agency, national association) with an ongoing relationship to and expertise in the rulemaking process itself, distinct from subject-matter expertise

proposals.name: NGO action-alert templated phrasing
proposals.instruction: Score the presence of stock activist/action-alert phrasing typical of NGO mass-comment campaign tools: formulaic gratitude closings ('THANK YOU for your commitment to...'), superlative-modified statements of position ('I HIGHLY support...', 'I strongly urge...'), and emphatic capitalized keywords, especially combined with a short, largely interchangeable one-fact-plus-a-plea structure. 10 = the comment strongly exhibits this templated activist register. 0 = the comment shows no such stock phrasing.
proposals.rationale: ROW R01 ('PLEASE continue the current moratorium... IF extending this moratorium saves the life of even one more precious turtle', dense_pct=.429/card_pct=.976) and ROW R17 ('I applaud HHS for proposing this regulation... I urge HHS to ensure clear and conspicuous notice...', dense_pct=.517/card_pct=.972) both show this register and score extremely high on card but only mid-range on dense. ROW R13 shows the same closing/superlative register but paired with added factual elaboration (dense_pct=.687), suggesting the template marker itself, not the underlying content, is what the scorecard is rewarding independent of dense's judgment.
proposals.upstream_parent: comment was generated or guided by an NGO/advocacy-group mass-comment campaign tool (e.g. a pre-filled web action alert) that supplies stock phrasing for the submitter to personalize

proposals.name: Embedded formal citation within personal-voice prose
proposals.instruction: Score whether the comment juxtaposes an otherwise personal, informal, first-person narrative voice with one or more embedded formal legal or scholarly citations (e.g. a full case citation, a parenthetical citation to a named organization, a footnoted source) that read as though inserted by someone other than the narrating voice. 10 = a clear formal citation is embedded within personal/informal prose, creating a register shift. 0 = no such embedded citation is present, or the whole comment is uniformly formal or uniformly informal with no citations at all.
proposals.rationale: ROW R08 (a first-person FEMA fire-claim comment styled as a personal grievance, containing a full case citation 'Castillo v. City of Las Vegas, 195 P.3d 870, 875 (N.M. Ct. App. 2008)' embedded mid-argument, dense_pct=.631) and ROW R43 (a personal-register comment about the Hawaiian Hawk that embeds parenthetical citations '(American Bird Conservancy)', '(Honolulu Zoo Society)' like footnotes in a school paper, dense_pct=.880) both show this register-shift citation pattern paired with high dense scores; the Castillo citation is also substantively on-point for R08's argument, so the upstream factor plausibly improves genuine merit too.
proposals.upstream_parent: the comment received legal or research assistance (e.g. an attorney or claims law firm representing a claimant, or a teacher/librarian helping a student) that supplied one or more specific supporting citations without otherwise rewriting the submitter's voice

proposals.name: Direct interrogative questions addressed to the agency
proposals.instruction: Score the density and prominence of direct questions posed TO the agency/regulator (e.g. 'What is...?', 'Is this sufficient...?', 'Why do we have to...?') as the comment's primary rhetorical mode, as opposed to declarative statements of position or argument. 10 = the comment is structured mainly as a sequence of direct questions to the regulator. 0 = the comment contains no direct questions to the agency at all.
proposals.rationale: ROW R06 ('Are these all Ameri-King units...? What is the failure rate of the AK-450...?', dense_pct=.407), ROW R22 ('What is the practical legal definition and application of an affirmation...?', dense_pct=.275), and ROW R34 ('Is this sufficient for NOAA to monitor...? Would CBP...?', dense_pct=.166) all rely heavily on this interrogative technique and cluster at the low end of dense despite scoring moderately-to-highly on card (.875, .758, .618 respectively).
proposals.upstream_parent: comment was drafted (often by counsel or policy staff) partly to build an administrative record for potential future litigation -- posing pointed questions on the record rather than persuading -- a technique associated with regulated-industry or advocacy-org legal strategy

proposals.name: Named agency official addressed with internal office routing detail
proposals.instruction: Score how precisely the comment targets a specific human inside the agency, judging ONLY the addressing apparatus and never the argument. 10 = the salutation names an individual official AND pins their exact internal unit or mail routing (office code, division, branch, room, mailstop), and/or the letter carries an internal cc distribution list of named staff; first-name familiarity in the salutation ('Dear Brian;') sits at the very top of the range. 5 = a named official with only a generic title and public mailing address. 0 = 'To Whom It May Concern', 'Dear Sir or Madam', 'Docket Clerk', or no addressee at all. Ignore how long or how technical the comment is.
proposals.rationale: R32 addresses 'Mr. Brian Kierstead, Aerospace Engineer, Engine Certification Office, ANE-142' and then slips into 'Dear Brian;'. R02 writes to the named Deputy Administrator and recounts a meeting with his Office of Vehicle Safety Compliance staff. R10 names a Senior Economist and her exact division; R20 carries a nine-name internal cc list. Against these, R35 opens 'To Wom It May Concern' and R04 'Dear Sir or Madam'. Knowing the right person's name is a fact about access and prior contact, not about whether the reasoning inside is sound - but it is exactly the kind of surface a dense reader picks up as 'this writer is inside the process'. Marked mixed because an office with the relationship often also has the expertise.
proposals.upstream_parent: An existing working relationship between the submitter and the specific agency office - the submitter already knows, by name, who owns this docket.

proposals.name: Continuity references to prior filings, meetings, or pending petitions
proposals.instruction: Score how strongly the comment presents itself as one turn in an ongoing exchange rather than a first and only contact. 10 = it explicitly cites its own earlier comment letters on related dockets, a pending petition it is supplementing, a dated meeting with agency staff, or an emailed agency request it is answering, with dates. 5 = a vague gesture at past involvement ('we have long supported', 'we continue to be on the record'). 0 = nothing in the text indicates the writer has ever contacted this agency before. Score the continuity references only; do not reward the substance being continued.
proposals.rationale: R02 supplements a September 27, 2019 petition and reports what was said at a December 17, 2020 meeting held in response to a December 7 agency email. R41 notes the Stakeholders 'previously submitted a comment letter' on both the 2014 and 2015 drafts. R57 writes 'As I stated in my May 10, 2018 letter to you', and R39 says 'SSA continues to be on the record'. Whether a commenter has a back-catalogue with the agency is a property of the relationship, not of this comment's merit; but it leaves a very legible textual trace. Mixed because repeat players also accumulate genuine subject knowledge.
proposals.upstream_parent: Repeat-player status: a standing, multi-round relationship with the agency built from prior dockets, petitions, and staff meetings.

proposals.name: Coordination fingerprints: naming other commenters and incorporating their filings
proposals.instruction: Score how much the text reveals that the writer has read the rest of the docket and is acting in concert with others. 10 = the comment names other submitters and answers them directly, adopts or incorporates another organization's comments by reference, is labeled a joint or 'et al.' submission, or is one numbered piece of a multi-part batch with a master index of exhibits. 5 = it points readers to allied organizations without engaging them. 0 = the comment shows no awareness that anyone else is commenting. Judge coordination evidence only, not the quality of the coordinated position.
proposals.rationale: R55 'hereby adopts and incorporates by reference' the comments of LMOGA, the American Chemistry Council and LDEQ. R30 opens 'These comments primarily respond to comments submitted by GE Avionics'. R31 refers the Service to separate letters from three named partner organizations. R51 is literally '[Batch 11 of 18]' of 'joint comments submitted by Natural Resources Defense Council et al.' with a master index of attachments. Being inside a campaign changes how a filing looks and how it lands, independently of the argument it makes. Mixed: coalitions really do marshal evidence a lone writer could not.
proposals.upstream_parent: Membership in a coordinated advocacy campaign or industry coalition operating a shared docket strategy with division of labour.

proposals.name: Constituency-scale claims used as standing
proposals.instruction: Score how prominently and how quantitatively the writer states whom they speak for and how big that constituency is. 10 = an early passage puts hard numbers on the represented base - member counts, employee or job totals, market or capacity share, facility counts, revenue share, number of signatories. 5 = a qualitative representational claim with no figures ('the national voice for the industry'). 0 = no representational claim at all; the writer speaks only for themselves and offers no scale figures. Do not credit numbers used as evidence about the rule; only numbers used to establish who the writer is.
proposals.rationale: R10 leads with 'nearly 440 chemical distributors', '85% of the chemical distribution capacity', '155,000 direct and indirect jobs'. R33 opens with 'approximately 20,000 miners in the United States and an equivalent number in Canada'. R09 begins 'I represent 35,000 retired teachers'. R31 is 'comprised of 120 career academics, conservationists, and biologists'. Headcount is a fact about the submitter's organisational weight, not about the comment; it is a pure standing signal that a text-reading model can nonetheless see. Mixed because well-resourced bodies also write better-evidenced comments.
proposals.upstream_parent: Organizational resources and a dues-paying membership base, deployed as a substitute for argument-level standing.

proposals.name: Counsel-drafted citation and definition conventions
proposals.instruction: Score the density of courtroom drafting habits in the prose. 10 = statutory pincites with reporter parentheticals, 'et seq.', '(West)', Federal Register citations in full form including '(to be codified at ...)', case citations with page pincites, numbered footnotes carrying authority, defined terms introduced in quotation marks with parentheticals such as ('the IFR') or ('the Code'), and conformed '/s/' signatures. 5 = occasional formal citations without the defined-term and footnote machinery. 0 = no citations, no defined terms, no footnotes, plain lay prose. Score the drafting conventions, not whether the cited authority actually supports anything.
proposals.rationale: R08 (law students) writes '16 U.S.C.A. Sec. 1801 et seq. (West)' and '83 Fed. Reg. 2412 (proposed Jan. 17, 2018) (to be codified at 50 C.F.R. pt. 300)'. R28 defines 'the Code' and 'the Proposed Regulations', footnotes its own self-description and closes with two '/s/' blocks. R24 pincites Sec. 6050X(a)(2)(B) precisely. R15, a lay fire claimant, nonetheless pincites 'Castillo v. City of Las Vegas, 195 P.3d 870, 875 (N.M. Ct. App. 2008)'. Whether a lawyer held the pen is upstream of the text and orthogonal to whether the point is right. Mixed: counsel also catch real legal defects.
proposals.upstream_parent: Drafting by a lawyer - outside counsel, an in-house general counsel's office, or a law-school clinic - rather than by the party in interest.

proposals.name: Internal comment-form scaffolding keyed to rule numbering
proposals.instruction: Score how much the comment reads as an institutional review artifact rather than composed prose. 10 = repeated fixed-heading blocks such as 'Comment No. 1 / Page-Paragraph-Section / Comment Type: Non-Concur / What is the proposed requirement? / Rationale', an enclosure explicitly supplied 'in tabular format', or an exhaustive march down the rule's own subpart and section numbers with one item per paragraph. 5 = numbered headings that track the rule loosely. 0 = free-form prose with no scaffolding and no section-keyed enumeration. Score the scaffolding only; a scaffolded comment may be shallow and an unscaffolded one deep.
proposals.rationale: R23 files a document headed 'DISPOSITION OF PUBLIC COMMENTS' with 'Comment No.1 / Comment Type: Non-Concur / What is the FAA's proposed requirement or text? / Rationale'. R12 states 'Specific comments on the collection activity are included in the table below' and then runs numbered General and Specific blocks. R20 submits 'comments in the enclosure in tabular format' behind a bulleted support/oppose summary. R15 walks 'Subpart A Section 296.4 ... Subpart C 296.21(c)(2) ... Subpart D Section 296.31' one line at a time. The shape is a fingerprint of the submitter's internal process, not of insight. Mixed: an SME review pass does raise real accuracy.
proposals.upstream_parent: An internal multi-reviewer clearance workflow in which several subject-matter experts fill a standard comment-collection template that is then filed largely verbatim.

proposals.name: Alphanumeric part, model, and service-bulletin identifier density
proposals.instruction: Score how far the comment's substance rests on proprietary alphanumeric designators that only the manufacturer and the agency can resolve. 10 = the argument is unreadable without the manufacturer's own documents, e.g. engine or model codes ('V2527E-A5', 'RB211-524B4-02'), service bulletins with revision levels ('SB 25-1111432 Rev.002', '737-71-1937 RB'), and figure or paragraph pointers inside those bulletins. 5 = a few regulation-level identifiers only (a CFR part, an FMVSS number). 0 = no part, model, or bulletin identifiers anywhere. Score identifier density, not correctness.
proposals.rationale: R29 argues entirely from Figures 3 and 4 of 'Meggitt SB 25-1111432 Rev.002' and attaches the bulletin. R32 asks that 'V2525-D5, V2528-D5 and V2531-E5' be struck from applicability, citing NMSB V2500-ENG-72-0671. R18 turns on 'Boeing Special Attention Requirements Bulletin 737-71-1937 RB' versus '737-78-1106 RB'; R46 on 'RB211-524B4-02'. This is a marker of who the submitter is and what genre of docket they are in - the comment could be a decisive engineering correction or a trivial applicability nit and look identical. Mixed: engineering departments hold facts nobody else has.
proposals.upstream_parent: The submitter is a regulated manufacturer or operator with an engineering-compliance department, filing into an airworthiness-directive-style docket that functions as bilateral engineering negotiation rather than public policy debate.

proposals.name: Named-organism decline-and-extinction register
proposals.instruction: Score how far the comment is written in the conservation register centred on named living creatures. 10 = one or more species are named (common or scientific) and the text runs on decline, extinction risk, habitat, nesting or breeding, bleaching, parasitism, biodiversity, and ecosystem loss. 5 = environmental subject matter with no named organism. 0 = no organism named and no conservation vocabulary at all. Score register and topic only; a comment in this register may contain no new information and one outside it may contain a great deal.
proposals.rationale: R14 (twelve threatened corals), R19 (Kirtland's Warbler and cowbird parasitism), R34 (Hawaiian Hawk, native forest, ROD dieback), R05 (Sacramento Mountains checkerspot butterfly) and R40 (sihek / Guam kingfisher) all sit squarely in this register, and several of them - R05 and R34 in particular - are essentially unsourced general natural history that adds no fact the agency lacks. Topic composition of the mining pool is not merit, so a channel that fires on species vocabulary is predictive-without-quality by construction.
proposals.upstream_parent: Docket genre - species-listing and critical-habitat rulemakings recruit a distinctive writer population and are processed through a distinctive agency workflow, independent of any individual comment's content.

proposals.name: Paper or image submission provenance visible as OCR debris
proposals.instruction: Score how visibly the text is a machine transcription of a scanned page rather than digital-native text. 10 = pervasive transcription damage - '(cid:9)' tokens, one-word-per-line spacing with stray soft hyphens, mangled letters inside real words ('Califomia', 'V/ater', 'LACIDHS', 'Alter!' for 'Alteri'), letterhead and marginalia fragments spliced mid-sentence, page furniture, postmark or envelope text interleaved with prose. 5 = occasional artifacts (a few '(cid:9)' or a broken header). 0 = clean text with no transcription damage. Score the damage only; never penalise or reward the argument that survives it.
proposals.rationale: R01 is a postmarked handwritten envelope transcribed into near-nonsense ('EPA DOCKET CENTER (cid:9)', 'NOV 2 1 2019'). R04 renders every single word on its own line with soft hyphens. R41 shows 'Califomia' and 'V/ater' throughout. R25 splices letterhead fragments into mid-sentence text ('MalF.Yex 4c, @D- 0.'). R60 carries '(cid:9)' and 'Sean Alter!'. Nothing about scanner quality or the postal route is evidence of merit, yet it saturates the text a reader actually sees.
proposals.upstream_parent: The submission channel itself - paper mailed to the docket centre, or a scanned image PDF, rather than a digital-native filing - which is a proxy for era, for postal versus electronic routing, and for the submitter's document-production infrastructure.

proposals.name: Evidence no editor or intermediary touched the text
proposals.instruction: Score how plainly the text is unmediated first-person writing that no professional editor or communications staffer passed over. Evidence for a high score: uncorrected typos and misspellings, caps-lock emphasis, exclamation marks, sarcasm or rhetorical questions aimed at the agency, run-on asides, and personal rather than institutional identifiers offered as credentials (years in a trade, a named vessel or aircraft or farm, a home town, a signature with no organisational title). 10 = several of these, unmistakably. 0 = uniformly copy-edited third-person institutional prose with a titled signature block and no typographic slips. Score the mediation evidence, not whether the writer is right.
