proposals.rationale: R19 writes 'insuffucient' and 'Unitrd States'; R38 is openly sarcastic ('How dare such people so arrogantly expect their homes ... to simply be made whole again, eh?'); R57 asks 'who is the USDA representing - Turkey??' and signs 'Fourth Generation Family Farmer'; R52 shouts 'It makes NO SENSE' and offers thirty years of charter fishing as its credential; R35 opens 'To Wom It May Concern' from a Nantucket address; R27 is ungrammatical end to end. Whether a comment passed an editor's desk is upstream of the words and says nothing about whether the point is correct. Marked mixed honestly: an editing pass does make an argument clearer, and unmediated writers do supply first-hand facts.
proposals.upstream_parent: Absence of a professional editor, communications shop, or any intermediary between the writer and the docket - the writer is a directly affected individual filing on their own behalf.

proposals.name: Organizational scale claims
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment prominently gives concrete membership, geographic, facility, staffing, revenue, or population-reach figures; score 0 when it contains no organizational-scale self-description.
proposals.rationale: Quantified institutional scale appears in R07, R20, R22, and R36, potentially cueing dense attention independently of the comment’s actual reasoning.
proposals.upstream_parent: organizational resources and perceived representativeness

proposals.name: Agency relationship continuity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the text signals prior meetings, collaboration, prior submissions, ongoing agency contacts, or direct responses to agency questions; score 0 when it presents itself as a one-off submission with no continuity cues.
proposals.rationale: R17 describes a long partnership with DOT, while R20 cites earlier submissions and R21 reports a meeting with NHTSA staff.
proposals.upstream_parent: existing relationships with agency personnel and repeated access

proposals.name: Credential and title stacking
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the author or signatories display multiple senior titles, degrees, certifications, fellowships, or formal appointments; score 0 when no author credentials or status markers appear.
proposals.rationale: R41 lists extensive aviation credentials and experience, while R57 and R60 foreground multiple advanced credentials and institutional appointments.
proposals.upstream_parent: submitter seniority and sector standing

proposals.name: Coalition coordination footprint
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment identifies a joint campaign, many member organizations, numerous signatories, or a named coalition; score 0 when it is plainly submitted by one unaffiliated individual.
proposals.rationale: R08 is part of joint comments with an attachment master index, R20 lists many stakeholder entities, and R28 describes a 120-person expert working group.
proposals.upstream_parent: coordinated advocacy campaign and coalition resources

proposals.name: Professional document production
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the text visibly includes formal letterhead, pagination, branded covers, attachment inventories, slide decks, exhibits, or other costly production artifacts; score 0 when it is plain unformatted prose without documentary apparatus.
proposals.rationale: R03, R08, R14, R21, and R40 contain highly produced letters, indexed attachments, service-bulletin material, or presentation slides that may cue density independent of substance.
proposals.upstream_parent: professional editing, administrative capacity, and submission resources

proposals.name: Lifecycle engagement markers
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment references earlier drafts, prior comments, extensions, supplemental material, meetings, responses to other commenters, or delayed transmission; score 0 when it gives no sign of broader docket engagement.
proposals.rationale: R17 requests extra time after internal coordination, R19 responds to GE Avionics, R21 supplements an earlier petition after an agency inquiry, and R47 apologizes for late delivery.
proposals.upstream_parent: comment timing, repeated participation, and docket-lifecycle position

proposals.name: Operational technical granularity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment supplies numerous model numbers, paragraph-level edits, measurements, test results, compliance sequences, or implementation constraints; score 0 when it offers only broad conclusions without operational detail.
proposals.rationale: R14, R21, R40, R46, and R51 provide unusually detailed equipment identifiers, measurements, testing, maintenance pathways, and implementation timelines.
proposals.upstream_parent: access to technical staff, proprietary records, and engineering resources

proposals.name: Embedded constituency experience
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the author explicitly states long tenure, personal operation, affected employment, direct exposure, or responsibility for a named constituency and connects it to the topic; score 0 when no lived or sector connection is claimed.
proposals.rationale: R01 cites continuous vessel monitoring, R25 describes training and flight experience, R39 cites 30 years of fishing, and R44 identifies the author as a fourth-generation farmer.
proposals.upstream_parent: sector embeddedness and constituency standing

proposals.name: Universal-benefit framing
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment relies heavily on broad appeals to public good, future generations, ecosystem health, saving species, or general moral necessity without discussing specific mechanisms or tradeoffs; score 0 when it avoids generalized value language and stays narrowly provision-specific.
proposals.rationale: R12, R16, R27, R33, and R58 repeatedly use sweeping protection and public-benefit claims while providing little rule-specific analysis, a rhetorical pattern that may attract dense scoring without demonstrating merit.
proposals.upstream_parent: surface-only

proposals.name: Record-building cross-references
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment constructs a formal record through dense statutory or regulatory references, quoted provisions, footnotes, incorporated comments, docket citations, or linked authorities; score 0 when it contains no such formal cross-reference structure.
proposals.rationale: R23 uses statutory authorities and incorporated testimony, R37 incorporates multiple organizations’ comments, R53 builds arguments around statutory text, and R59 cites specific tax provisions and reporting thresholds.
proposals.upstream_parent: professional legal advocacy and access to counsel

proposals.name: First-person lived experience
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment foregrounds the writer's personal work, use, loss, observations, or stake; score 0 when it is entirely impersonal and institutional or technical.
proposals.rationale: Personal exposure can make prose vivid and memorable without validating its policy claims. Examples include the autobiographical accounts in R05 and R19, and the victim narrative in R42.
proposals.upstream_parent: Submitter's direct exposure to the regulated activity and grassroots testimonial mobilization

proposals.name: Credential and status parade
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the opening prominently lists multiple degrees, certifications, fellowships, offices, titles, or years of experience; score 0 when no status or expertise signals appear.
proposals.rationale: Status signaling can attract model attention independently of the argument's merit. R05 lists extensive aviation credentials, while R14 foregrounds professorship, fellowship, and international expertise.
proposals.upstream_parent: Submitter's professional seniority, standing, and access to policymakers

proposals.name: Coalition scale signaling
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment emphasizes membership counts, geographic reach, signatories, or numerous represented organizations; score 0 when it comes from an unrepresented individual with no constituency claims.
proposals.rationale: Large constituencies may increase perceived importance without making the submitted reasoning better. This fingerprint is prominent in R44's 120-member working group and R56's representation of 29 elected sheriffs.
proposals.upstream_parent: Organizational mobilization capacity and representational standing

proposals.name: Emotional advocacy intensity
proposals.instruction: Score 10 for repeated alarm, outrage, moral condemnation, emphatic praise, all-caps, exclamation marks, or vivid metaphors; score 0 for consistently restrained, neutral prose.
proposals.rationale: Emotion can make a comment salient while supplying no additional support for its claims. R22 uses highly charged language about pets and death, and R42 describes a 'crafty bureaucrat's tool' and catastrophic ruin.
proposals.upstream_parent: Advocacy-campaign messaging norms

proposals.name: Testimonial narrative framing
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment unfolds as a story about a person, place, community, or unfolding harm before reaching its request; score 0 when it begins with a compact docket-specific issue list or technical disposition table.
proposals.rationale: Narrative structure can create memorability and apparent human importance without improving policy analysis. R19 begins with school and diving experiences, while R36 frames the issue through a fourth-generation farmer's personal situation.
proposals.upstream_parent: Grassroots or community mobilization using testimonial storytelling

proposals.name: Multi-issue agenda bundling
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when one comment combines several related policy campaigns, controversies, or reform demands into a broad agenda; score 0 when it addresses one narrowly defined provision or implementation question.
proposals.rationale: Breadth can look substantive to a dense reader while partly reflecting an organization's preexisting agenda rather than relevance to the docket. R07 bundles nitrate, genetic-engineering, and poultry-production demands; R10 combines numerous sanctuary, climate, wildlife, and economic themes.
proposals.upstream_parent: Lobbying organizations pursuing a standing agenda across multiple rulemakings

proposals.name: Professional document apparatus
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the submission contains elaborate exhibits, master indexes, slide decks, service-bulletin reproductions, revision histories, or attachment-heavy packaging; score 0 for a plain standalone comment with no document-production signals.
proposals.rationale: Packaging can signal seriousness and raise salience even when the underlying claim is weak or routine. R39 supplies a large indexed attachment library, while R60 appends a polished eleven-slide technical presentation.
proposals.upstream_parent: Availability of lawyers, engineers, consultants, and professional document-production resources

proposals.name: Litigation posture
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment frames the issue through court cases, incorporation by reference, administrative-record preservation, constitutional or APA objections, or accusations of unlawful agency action; score 0 when it contains no adversarial legal posture.
proposals.rationale: A litigation-oriented voice may appear consequential because it highlights legal vulnerability, not because its policy reasoning is sound. R36 invokes a court case and alleged unlawful board conduct, while R55 argues appointments-clause and APA issues.
proposals.upstream_parent: Legal counsel involvement and defensive preparation for regulatory litigation

proposals.name: Agency-relationship cues
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment mentions prior meetings, ongoing collaboration, earlier submissions, established partnerships, or direct exchanges with agency personnel; score 0 when it has only a generic salutation and no relationship history.
proposals.rationale: Relationship language can make a submission seem institutionally consequential without adding evidence about the proposal. R23 emphasizes a longstanding AASHTO-DOT partnership, R26 cites earlier submissions, and R60 reports a meeting with NHTSA staff.
proposals.upstream_parent: Existing relationships and insider access within the agency or docket lifecycle

proposals.name: Tailored-relief seeking
proposals.instruction: Score 10 when the comment seeks a submitter-specific exemption, extension, participation opportunity, applicability carve-out, phased schedule, or cost adjustment; score 0 when it requests only general policy treatment.
proposals.rationale: A concrete self-interested ask can produce a strong salience signal even when the requested exception is not substantively justified. R06 requests a 60-month exemption extension, R24 seeks a utilization-based compliance schedule, and R30 requests inclusion in future pricing models.
proposals.upstream_parent: Submitter's material exposure and lobbying for individualized regulatory relief
